name: Growing Neural Cellular Automata
principle: A shared local neural update rule evolves cell states from a seed into a target pattern; hidden channels support distributed, regenerative developmental dynamics.
learning_rule: Per cell, perceive state and Sobel-neighbor features; update h_i <- h_i + MLP(perception(h)_i), with stochastic update dropout; optimize shared MLP parameters by BPTT to minimize pixelwise L2 loss against target RGBA. Pool and damage augmentation train persistence/regeneration.
backprop_notes: Backpropagation through time trains shared cellular update-rule weights using image reconstruction loss; no RL reward is involved, but the objective is externally specified target supervision.
limitations: Demonstrations are target-image generation, not an agent benchmark; no Crafter result.
Learning objective is supervised and uses BPTT, failing the no-backprop GENESIS criterion.
notes: Distill full text opened; qualitative demonstrations only, no numerical agent benchmark.

name: Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer (POET)

sources.title: Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer (POET): Endlessly Generating Increasingly Complex and Diverse Learning Environments and Their Solutions

principle: Maintains environment-agent pairs, mutates environments, optimizes each agent with evolution strategies, and transfers agents across environments when they improve the resident solution.
learning_rule: For each environment, evaluate policy parameter perturbations and update policy weights with rank-normalized ES returns (Adam in paper); mutate obstacle parameters and retain eligible environments by solved/unsolved score range; periodically transfer the best-performing policy into another environment.
learning_signals: extrinsic: environment task return used for ES optimization, environment eligibility and transfer selection
backprop_notes: Policy parameters are updated by evolution strategies from sampled perturbations and returns; paper states not backpropagation.

benchmarks.metric: score (paper's success threshold 230; direct ES controls on illustrated hard environments)
benchmarks.source: arXiv:1901.01753 full text, comparison reports direct-ES scores 17.9, 39.6, 13.6 vs POET success threshold 230; exact table unavailable in fetched extract

limitations: Relies on external task returns, so does not meet reward-free criterion.
The opened full-text extract did not provide a code URL; code publication not verified.

name: PAIRED (Protagonist Antagonist Induced Regret Environment Design)

sources.title: Emergent Complexity and Zero-shot Transfer via Unsupervised Environment Design

principle: An adversary generates structured environments to maximize regret between a protagonist and antagonist; the protagonist's learning difficulty drives a curriculum of solvable but challenging tasks.
learning_rule: Adversary maximizes regret R_adv = V_antagonist - V_protagonist (with environment validity constraints); train protagonist and antagonist with underlying RL objectives. Specific update details not verified from abstract.
learning_signals: extrinsic/task reward for protagonist and antagonist returns
backprop_notes: PAIRED is a curriculum/environment-design framework, not a standalone learner; its regret uses the agents' reward returns and underlying policy optimizer may use backprop. Exact policy gradient implementation not verified from abstract/full-text fetch.
limitations: The fetched abstract confirms transfer claims but has no numeric/table details.
Depends on task returns; not reward-free.
notes: Full-text/source fetch not successfully verified; do not infer numerical results.

name: Prioritized Level Replay (PLR)
principle: Prioritizes replay of procedurally generated levels estimated to have high future learning potential, mixing level score and staleness to improve sample efficiency and generalization.
learning_rule: Compute a level score from mean absolute GAE over its latest trajectory; rank-prioritize scores and mix with staleness-based sampling. The underlying PPO learner updates policy/value parameters from rewards; PLR selects levels rather than prescribing the learner update.
learning_signals: extrinsic: environment returns used to compute GAE/value learning potential
curriculum: absolute GAE and level staleness
backprop_notes: PLR itself has no parameter-gradient rule; experiments use PPO, whose policy/value networks are gradient-trained. PLR's GAE score is reward-dependent.

benchmarks.metric: normalized test return (% of uniform baseline)
normalized test return (% of uniform baseline)

limitations: Curriculum signal is derived from task reward and value/GAE estimates.
Results depend on underlying RL agent and benchmark's procedural levels.
notes: arXiv HTML v4 opened. Tables 2 and 4: PLR normalized Procgen test returns cited above; UCB-DrAC+PLR reaches 176.4% easy and 182.9% hard, not attributed to PLR alone.

name: Intrinsically Motivated Goal Exploration Processes (IMGEP)

sources.title: Intrinsically Motivated Goal Exploration Processes with Automatic Curriculum Learning

principle: An agent explores a goal space by selecting goals with intrinsic progress/reward, learning goal-conditioned policies incrementally, and reusing experience across goals; AMB uses a population-based policy and object-centered modularity.
learning_rule: Select goal g_t using intrinsic goal-selection score; execute goal-conditioned policy, observe outcome and update goal-conditioned policy/model from experience; details differ by IMGEP variant and were not specified in opened abstract.
learning_signals: intrinsic: goal novelty/progress or competence-related goal-selection reward (variant-dependent)
no task reward necessary in stated intrinsically motivated setup
backprop_notes: IMGEP is a framework, not one learner; the abstract does not specify optimizer. Goal-conditioned policies may be trained with gradient methods, while the intrinsic goal selector is not necessarily gradient-based; exact implementation unverified.
limitations: Abstract lacks exact learning equations, optimizer, code link, and numeric results.
Some variants may use task reward or gradient-trained policies; cannot claim universal no-reward/no-backprop.
notes: arXiv abstract opened; qualitative robot exploration/high-dimensional goal-space claims only; no numeric results extracted.

name: MAP-Elites

sources.title: Illuminating Search Spaces by Mapping Elites

principle: Partitions a user-defined behavioral descriptor space into cells and stores the highest-quality solution found in each cell, producing a diverse archive of strong solutions.
learning_rule: Initialize archive; repeatedly select an archived elite, mutate/search its candidate parameters, evaluate quality f(x) and descriptor b(x), then replace the corresponding cell if the candidate has higher quality.
backprop_notes: MAP-Elites is an outer evolutionary search/archive algorithm and does not require backpropagation; candidate quality may be a task reward or another objective, and the inner candidate representation can vary.
limitations: Requires a hand-chosen quality objective and behavior descriptors; quality may be an external reward.
No Crafter result or quantitative table verified from fetched abstract.
Abstract page did not include official code repository.
notes: Abstract reports soft-robot and modular neural-network demonstrations and comparison claim, but no numeric/table results captured.
